public_rationale: The records establish an old debate about systematicity and a modern direction-sensitive generalization failure. They do not establish that the same symmetry error persisted across decades. Treating every systematicity concern as the same failure would decide the claim through an interpretation Marcus did not specify.
limitations: Failure to locate a matching historical experiment is not evidence that none exists.
The broader claim that systematicity has been debated for decades is easier to establish than this claim about a persistent error.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The symmetry failure is a big, persistent error in neural networks that has endured for decades.

statement.excerpt: This symmetry fail is mighty big, a mighty persistent error that has endured for decades.
statement.document_title: Elegant and powerful new result that seriously undermines large language models

our_interpretation: The checkable core is recurrence of comparable symmetry or reversal-generalization failures across neural-network generations separated by at least twenty years.
Persistence does not require every intervening model to fail or an unchanged underlying mechanism.
The historical period begins with the 1980s discussion named in the surrounding text and ends at the post.
Mighty big is an assessment of importance, not a supplied quantitative threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Independent primary records establish comparable relational reversal failures in neural networks at dates at least twenty years apart, including the contemporary endpoint.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The historical records alleged to demonstrate the earlier failure instead establish that it did not occur or concerned a materially different phenomenon, with the claimed continuity thereby disproved.
